summary: Nogapendekin alfa inbakicept (Anktiva) is an IL-15 receptor agonist given intravesically with BCG for adults with BCG-unresponsive non-muscle invasive bladder cancer with carcinoma in situ, with or without papillary tumors. The dose is 400 mcg with BCG once weekly for a 6-week induction (repeatable once if month-3 response is incomplete), followed by 3-week maintenance courses at months 4, 7, 10, 13, and 19. It expands NK, CD8+, and memory T cells without expanding regulatory T cells. Systemic exposure is negligible; toxicity is local bladder irritation plus BCG effects (dysuria, hematuria, frequency, urgency, UTI, chills, fever). The key warning is that delaying cystectomy while disease persists can lead to lethal metastatic bladder cancer.
indications: In combination with Bacillus Calmette-Guerin (BCG) for adult patients with BCG-unresponsive non-muscle invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC) with carcinoma in situ (CIS) with or without papillary tumors

admin: For intravesical use only after dilution; do NOT give by subcutaneous, intravenous, or intramuscular routes
Complete the time from vial puncture to finished instillation within 2 hours; if the admixture is not used immediately, refrigerate at 2-8 C and use within 2 hours, then discard any unused portion
Instill the nogapendekin alfa inbakicept plus BCG admixture into the bladder by catheter, then remove the catheter and retain the admixture in the bladder for 2 hours before voiding
Patients unable to retain the suspension for 2 hours may void sooner; do not repeat the dose if voiding occurs early
Instruct patients to void while seated to avoid splashing, to stay well hydrated after treatment, and to report prolonged bladder symptoms or fever promptly
moa: Nogapendekin alfa inbakicept is an IL-15 receptor agonist. IL-15 normally signals through a heterotrimeric receptor (common gamma chain, beta chain, and the IL-15-specific alpha subunit) and is trans-presented by IL-15 receptor alpha to CD4+ and CD8+ T cells and NK cells. Binding of the drug to its receptor drives proliferation and activation of NK, CD8+, and memory T cells without expanding immunosuppressive regulatory T cells. In an immunocompetent bladder cancer model, intravesical drug alone or with BCG showed antitumor activity compared with BCG alone.

preg: Based on its mechanism of action, nogapendekin alfa inbakicept may cause fetal harm if systemic exposure occurs. There are no human pregnancy data and animal reproductive studies were not conducted. Advise pregnant women of the potential fetal risk and advise females of reproductive potential to use effective contraception during treatment and for 1 week after the last dose.
lact: There are no data on the presence of nogapendekin alfa inbakicept in human milk or its effects on the breastfed child or milk production. Consider the developmental and health benefits of breastfeeding along with the mother's clinical need and any potential adverse effects from the drug or the underlying condition.
renal: No dose adjustment is defined for renal impairment. Increased creatinine was among the most common laboratory abnormalities, so monitor serum creatinine and potassium during treatment.
hepatic: No dose adjustment is defined for hepatic impairment. Systemic exposure after intravesical dosing is negligible (below assay quantitation), so hepatic effects are not expected.

interactions.alcohol: No specific interaction is described; avoiding excess alcohol during treatment weeks is prudent.
interactions.diagnostics: Raises serum creatinine and potassium; red-tinged urine may occur in the first 24 hours after instillation.
interactions.food: Not applicable (intravesical); maintain adequate hydration after each treatment.

moderate: Nephrotoxic drugs (additive creatinine elevation; monitor renal function)

counsel: The medicine is placed into the bladder through a catheter and must stay in the bladder for 2 hours before you urinate; urinate while seated to avoid splashing
Drink fluids as advised after each treatment; pink-tinged urine in the first 24 hours can occur
Burning on urination, blood in urine, going often, urgency, bladder pain, chills, or fever are common; report prolonged or severe bladder symptoms or fever right away
Delaying bladder removal (cystectomy) while cancer persists can allow lethal metastatic bladder cancer to develop; discuss cystectomy with your urologist if response is incomplete
Use effective contraception during treatment and for 1 week after the last dose if pregnancy is possible

Vials refrigerated 2-8 C (36-46 F) in the original carton to protect from light; do not freeze or shake. Diluted admixture refrigerated 2-8 C and used within 2 hours; discard unused portion after 2 hours
pearls: Must always be given with BCG; it is not a single-agent therapy
Discuss cystectomy openly: delaying it while CIS persists risks lethal metastatic bladder cancer
The 2-hour bladder dwell and the 2-hour vial-puncture-to-instillation window are both strict

missed: Treatment is given in clinic on a weekly schedule, so there is no patient-managed missed dose. If an instillation visit is missed, the urology team will reschedule it. If the patient voids before completing the 2-hour bladder dwell, do not repeat the dose.
overdose: There is no overdose experience and no specific antidote. Expected effects are local bladder toxicity. Manage supportively with hydration, bladder symptom control, and monitoring of renal function and electrolytes. Contact Poison Help (1-800-222-1222).
